pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_usage/libs/periodComparison.ts:30 splits the doubled read by array position, but the dashboard series carries only observed days (src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/metrics.rs:1414 builds dates from non-empty buckets, no densify anywhere), so a quiet day shifts the cut and part of the current period is drawn and summed as the previous one

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_usage/libs/periodComparison.ts:30 positional split on a sparse series - the technique's named dense-series failure; same cut duplicated at src/features/overview/libs/computeTrends.ts:43, so the trend badges carry it too

src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/metrics.rs:1263 buckets the dashboard by UTC DATE(created_at) while the sibling Overview heatmap buckets by the client's local day (metrics.rs:2237), two zones feeding the same Overview surface

src/features/overview/sub_activity/libs/useExecutionMetrics.ts:39 passes a bare day count down (fetchDays) and each layer re-derives the range - the backend from datetime('now', '-N days') - instead of a resolved window value with bounds and zone
src/features/overview/sub_activity/libs/useExecutionMetrics.ts:99 compares flow metrics (cost, completed, failed counts), which the technique excludes: events have no as-of state, only a prior total
src/features/overview/libs/computeTrends.ts:116 trends are whole-population sums/averages of executions, not per-entity movement over a changing population

pairs.registryProposal: The ranked anchors for this context's deviation live outside its paths (useExecutionMetrics.ts in sub_activity, computeTrends.ts in overview/libs, metrics.rs in db): the context owns the splitter, not the read that makes it wrong. A verdict here cannot be fixed inside the context's own files; the comparison pipeline spans three contexts and the map has no context that owns it end to end.

pairs.registryProposal: Week start is hardcoded to Sunday (calendarHelpers.ts:62) in an app shipping 14 locales; canonical-zone-single-source says week alignment travels with the zone/locale decision but no decision rule says whether a consistent fixed weekday is acceptable or a deviation when locale varies. Worth one decision rule.
